"If one encounters demonic obstacles, suffers from illness, develops a goiter, or if the body and mind lack sincerity, leading to constant negligence; or if the body and mind are exhausted, if one violates the proper seasons, fails to follow the ritual rules, or occasionally fails to bathe; if one performs recitations and *homa* offerings that do not count toward the required number;
or if one practices with a concentrated mind according to the Dharma and performs recitations in accordance with the rules—these instances of counting should be recorded as the valid count."

"During the performance of homa, the recitation of mantras, and the invocation—within these three matters, the total number of mantra recitations must each be completed according to the ritual rules. Even if one has nearly reached the full count but falls short by a single recitation, and an obstacle arises, one must begin counting from the beginning again; if one acts without following the ritual rules, nothing will be accomplished."

"If one performs the recitation with the addition of ritual mantras during either the time of constructing a maṇḍala or during an eclipse of the sun or moon—during these two occasions—the merit will increase and accomplishment will be attained before long; of this there is no doubt."
"If one is at one of the eight great sacred stupas;
or at a site of past Buddhas and Bodhisattvas that is most supreme;
or on the fifteenth day of the first month, which is also a most excellent time;"
Alternatively, if one has previously performed the preliminary service (*puraścaraṇa*) for a mantra under a master, then at the time of recitation, it will be swiftly accomplished before long.
If, in a dream, one sees the Lord of Mantras (*mantranātha*) giving instructions, then by following those rules, one will also achieve accomplishment swiftly.

If the practitioner who recites the mantra performs offerings at a particularly exalted site for the Saṃgha, or applies exceptional sincerity during that time, then even if the required number of recitations has not been completed, the Lord of Mantras will be pleased by this excellence alone and grant accomplishment.

One should know that although the siddhi of this dharma is swift, it will not endure for long; for this reason, that which is attained after first completing the ritual service is said to be firm and stable.

During the initial period of service, one should perform extensive offerings; furthermore, during solar and lunar eclipses, as well as on the eighth and fifteenth days of the month, one should additionally present offerings to the hosts of ṛṣis and devas.

"As other schools state, one should perform all ritual activities, such as fasting and observances, on the aforementioned days; on this day, one should further increase the offerings to the Lord of the Mantra (Vidyārāja).

A flask filled with scented water and adorned with hanging flower branches—or taking an *argha* vessel, using the mantra of Amṛtakuṇḍalī—one should sprinkle it upon one's own crown, which can eliminate demonic obstacles.
Alternatively, on that day, one must additionally offer various foods and drinks, smear the maṇḍala, and perform *homa*, light lamps, and so forth."

If, within certain teachings, it is said that recitation alone will naturally bring about miraculous manifestations—such as when previously consecrated images, śarīra-relics, stūpas, and the like suddenly shake or emit flames—one should know that accomplishment will soon be swiftly attained.
"What are the signs when accomplishment is attained? They are as follows:
the body becomes light, the suffering of illness is forever eliminated, and superior wisdom is increased;
one manifests the majestic radiance of a fearless body."
In dreams at night, one constantly sees pure and true things, and the mind remains perpetually peaceful and secure;
during recitation and in all activities, no weariness arises, and a marvelous radiance issues from the body;
one feels reverence for generosity and honors those of noble virtue.
One should cultivate reverence for the Lord of Mantras.
When signs such as those described above appear at the time of accomplishment, one should know that these are the characteristics of success.
First, having completed the preliminary services, one should worship the deity according to the ritual rules, and further offer oblations and perform homa.
Once the preliminary service according to the prescribed number has been completed, one should next perform the recitation for *siddhi*, first making a request for the desired state within a dream.

Regarding the ritual procedure for preliminary service (*puraścaraṇa*): at the site where one intends to perform the recitation for *siddhi*, one should not move from that location. If various obstacles arise, one should continue the recitation as before and perform a penance (*daṇḍaka*); specifically, one should take the mantra of the Lord of the Family (*kuleśvara*) and recite it one thousand times.

Alternatively, one may recite the root mantra (*mūlamantra*) one hundred thousand times. If one departs from this [site], one must understand that the preliminary service is to be performed again as previously described.
While reciting with right mindfulness, if one suddenly errs and recites another mantra, and having realized the error, sincerely repents the transgression:
"Due to negligence, this error has occurred; may the Honored One forgive this fault."
Then, having prostrated with the crown of the head, one must again recite [the mantra] from the beginning.

If, due to mental negligence while in an impure place, one recites the root mantra, one should immediately recognize this and undergo purification. Upon returning to the place of recitation, one should recite the mantra of the Lord of the Family seven times, fast for one day during the half-month, and then consume the five pure substances after reciting the mantra over them one hundred and eight times.
By wearing these five purifiers, the impure food consumed during the half-month shall become pure, and the power of the mantra will increase.
The mantra for the Five Purifiers of the Buddha Family is:
*Namo bhagavate uṣṇīṣāya miḍi ṭi mi ra ce si me śāntigari svāhā.* The mantra for the Five Purifiers of the Lotus Family is:
“Namo ratnatrayāya | Namo āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahākāruṇikāya | Oṃ ya śuci svāhā. This is the fivefold purification mantra of the Vajra Family.

"Namaḥ ratnatrayāya | Namaḥ śakrāya vajrapāṇaye mahāyakṣasenāpataye | Oṃ śikhi śikhi ṛmmale prabhe prabhāsvare dṛḍhe dṛḍharābde prabhāvati svāhā. Take cow’s milk, curd, ghee, dung, and urine; recite the mantra over each separately one hundred and eight times, then place them together in one location. Recite the mantra once more one hundred and eight times while placing them in a vessel made of *palaśa* wood or the leaves of various milky trees.

Alternatively, stir the argha vessel with *kuśa* grass and recite the mantra one hundred and eight times; thereafter, squatting while facing east, drink three *sruk* at once, and in this manner, consume the medicine until it reaches one *droṇa*.
While taking the medicine, one should not engage in conversation.

During the time of recitation, if an image appears or a voice speaks, one should first discern the adversary; immediately recite the mantra and perform the mudrā of the Lord of the Family. If it is a māra at work, they will naturally retreat;
or if the speech that emerges differs from the original rite, one should know it to be the work of a māra.
If one utters words encouraging the commission of evil deeds, this too is the work of Māra.
"If you see an evil dream, you must first recite the mantra of the Mother of the Family (Kulīśvarī) one hundred and eight times;
if you do not first recite the mantra of the Mother of the Family, you must not perform any further recitation."
When reciting, one should not stop even if the count decreases; there is no fault if it increases.
One must follow the sequence of recitation as described above; otherwise, if one seeks siddhi while deviating from this method, it cannot be attained.

Chapter Nineteen: The Chapter on Radiant Manifestation from the Susiddhikara Sūtra Furthermore, I shall now explain the method for augmenting divine majesty and causing [the deities] to rejoice, whereby the mantras one upholds will be swiftly accomplished.

First, having prepared scented water and bathed one's body and hands, one should increase the various offerings during the auspicious hours of the day. Then, taking one hundred and eight *sumana* flowers, recite the mantra over each individual flower twenty-one times, seven times, or three times; first observing the number of syllables in the mantra, one should chant it and offer them to the deity.
Next, offer unguents and incense, as well as those of extraordinary fragrance.
Furthermore, offer food and drink as previously described, adding granulated sugar and curd.
Again, perform homa by burning one hundred and eight pieces of wood, each not exceeding the prescribed measure;
next, perform homa one hundred and eight times using a mixture of milk curds and honey;
next, perform homa one hundred and eight times using a mixture of ghee and curds with cooked non-glutinous rice.
These three *homa* rites should be performed for twenty-one days, or again for five days, or again for three days.
When these three days have concluded, one should take milk porridge mixed with cow’s ghee and perform *homa* one hundred and eight times;
when this is finished, one should take an *argha* vessel, recite the mantra over it one hundred and eight times, pour a small amount of water into it, and perform *homa*.
By performing these rites, the power of mantras is increased; that is to say, even if a mantra’s power is severed by another mantra, it will naturally regain its increase,
or the mantra may be either diminished or enhanced,
or if it has been obstructed by a *rākṣasa* mantra, it will no longer fail to function.
Whether the mantras are entangled with one another due to being bound,
or whether syllables have been added to the mantras—
may all such afflictions as these be entirely eliminated, so that [the mantra] may attain increased majesty.
"From among the medicinal herbs prescribed for all *homāḥ*, take any one of them and perform the *homā-mantra* for one hundred nights; thus, with joy, one shall attain increased power."

Furthermore, take various fragrances and blend them to form a fragrant paste, fashioning the form of the deity. Offer *mālatī* flowers and burn resinous tree incense or hard-wood incense. Recite the mantra one hundred and eight times during each of the three periods of the day; thus the mantra will become joyful and its power increased.
Fashion the form of this deity and place it upon a lotus leaf,
or a plantain leaf,
or a leaf from a milk-tree;

Alternatively, one may offer various grasses and leaves not only throughout the day and night, but continue doing so until the ritual is completed; then, according to the Dharma, one should perform the rite of dismissal (*visarjana*) and send them away to a great river.
For those who act according to these successive stages and this ritual procedure, the Honored Deity will be pleased and swiftly bestow *siddhi*.

Chapter Twenty: The Consecration of the Principal Deity (*Sussiddhikara-tantra*, Chapter on the Consecration of the Principal Deity, Number Twenty). "Furthermore, once the preliminary services have been completed, if one wishes to increase the majesty and power of the Lord of Mantras, one should consecrate him."

Take a vessel made of gold, silver, copper, or the like, or a new earthenware jar, and fill it with scented water. Place within it the five precious gems, flower petals, fruit, incense, and the five kinds of grain seeds, along with various unguents or powdered hard incenses. Tie a new piece of colored silk around the neck of the vessel, suspend it from the branch of a *śirīṣa* tree or a milky sap tree, and recite the mantra of the Lord of the Family or the mantra of the Mother of the Family one hundred and eight times. Thereafter, pour [the water] over the crown of the head of the Lord of Mantras.
One should fashion its form out of gold, or from *agaru* (sandalwood) or *candana* (sandalwood), place it upon a pedestal, and perform the consecration (*abhiṣeka*).

Once the consecration is completed, one should further present flowers, incense, and other offerings, or various ornaments and diverse articles of worship to make offerings to it. By performing *homa* and adding recitation (*japa*), one who acts in this manner will cause the deity to increase in power and swiftly attain *siddhi*.

"When the practitioner who has previously performed service performs the recitation, they should consecrate the deity; taking the *argha* vessel and visualizing the signs of the deity, they should perform the consecration.
Alternatively, when one has finished bathing oneself, one should again visualize the Lord of Mantras and perform the consecration three or seven times."
"One should not neglect or forget the prior service;

at times use ghee, and at other times fill a flask with honey, place seven precious gems within it, and hold it according to the ritual to consecrate the crown of the deity's head. Thus, the prayed-for aspiration will swiftly be fulfilled."
Chapter 21: The Chapter on Entreaty (*Adhyeṣaṇā*) from the Susiddhikara Sūtra. "Furthermore, the rules for the extensive practice of entreaty are as follows:
On the eighth, fourteenth, or fifteenth day of either the waxing or waning moon, or during an eclipse of the sun or moon, one should fast for one day;
or, having bathed for seven days to become pure, one should don new, clean garments."
Those who pray apart from this morning ritual should perform the supplication during the bright fortnight by reciting the *śāntika* mantra;

furthermore, at dusk, one should bathe with various decoctions and purify oneself using the mantra, removing all impurities and sprinkling [the water] upon the five places (*pañcavastu*). One should then make offerings according to the rite to the primary deity of the mantra.

Next, offer *argha* while reciting the mantra one hundred and eight times, scattering large blossoms of *jāti* flowers and sprinkling sandalwood-scented water as an offering. Furthermore, present an extensive food offering known as *unnāli-bhakṣa*, adding curd to the food and making a garland with *mālatī* flowers for the offering.
First, take cow ghee and perform one hundred and eight *homa* offerings;
next, use *śāla* wood for one hundred and eight *homa* offerings.

Have a young girl weave a cord using white cotton thread or cloth thread; for each mantra recited, tie one knot, thus tying seven knots. Then, recite the mantra seven times more and fasten it upon the upper arm or elbow. Lie on your left side and contemplate the Lord of Mantras.
"Once you have attained mastery over movement and remain at ease according to your will, seat yourself upon the throne, scatter flowers, and contemplate the form of the Honored One.
If, within your dreams, you see the Lord of your own family,
or the Lord of Mantras, or a Vidyārāja, you should know that these signs are the signs of accomplishment."
"Or they see the Triple Gem;
or they see various bodhisattvas;
or they see the fourfold assembly;"
Or one may see signs of siddhi from making offerings;
or see oneself reciting mantras and performing various rites;
or see oneself wearing pure white garments.
If one sees others coming to pay respect and make offerings, know that the supreme siddhi is close at hand.
Or one may see a mountain peak emerge;
or one may see oneself riding an elephant.
Some see them crossing great rivers and seas;
some see them ascending fruit trees;
some see them riding lions.
Some ride oxen, deer, or other such animals;
some ride flying geese, peacocks, or all manner of winged birds;
or they see beautiful women adorned with necklaces and holding flower vases in their hands.
Or one may see oneself walking along a path surrounded by fragrant flowers and canopies;
or one may see receiving elephants, horses, chariots, precious objects, and so forth—seeing such signs constitutes the sign of *siddhi*.
"Or, one may dream of obtaining flowers, fruits, roots, cow-ghee, milk, curd, rice blossoms, and other such items; these are the signs of the accomplishment (*siddhi*) of the medicinal substances.

During the preliminary service (*pūrvasevā*), dreams indicate the attainment of the medicinal substances and the acquisition of a rosary. One who obtains such signs should know that they must immediately perform the method of recitation (*japa*).
Alternatively, one may see oneself being perfumed with incense, or see oneself bathing and becoming pure."
Alternatively, if one sees oneself wearing necklaces and ornaments, upon seeing this sign, one should perform the recitation (*japa*), and *siddhi* will be swiftly attained.

Regarding the method for performing the recitation: take one hundred and eight *jāti* flowers and offer them while reciting the *Kulamātṛ-mantra* together with the root mantra one hundred and eight times.

Furthermore, take white sandalwood incense and recite the mantra over it one hundred and eight times. Then, knowing that this is a request for a dream, lie down to sleep at will; the root mantra itself shall manifest its signs.

Furthermore, take the *uśīra* herb, pound it, and mix it to fashion an image of the mantra-deity. Using soil from the anthill of *mīdurika* ants, fashion a vessel; fill it with cow’s milk and place the image within the milk, or alternatively, mix clarified butter (*sarpis*), milk, and honey, and place the image therein. Recite [the mantra] one hundred and eight times and perform offerings at the three periods of the day. By making such offerings, the deity will be pleased and signs of success will swiftly appear.

Furthermore, on the eighth, fourteenth, and fifteenth days of both the waxing and waning moon phases, or on the day of a solar or lunar eclipse, one should observe the fast by abstaining from food and extensively perform offerings. Using the two types of incense—the seven resinous aromatics (*saptaguggulu*) and the five solid aromatics (*pañcakaṭhina*)—one should recite the mantra once for each *homa* offering. Once the count reaches one thousand two hundred repetitions, the signs of the fulfillment of one’s prayers will swiftly appear before you.
If one performs the rules for invocation according to the ritual, accomplishment will be swiftly attained; seeing these signs, one should have no doubt. 22.
Chapter on Receiving Mantras, the Susiddhikara Sūtra, Chapter Twenty-Two: "Furthermore, the method for receiving mantras is explained in detail."

Kneeling with both knees on the ground, first perform extensive acts of giving before the Venerable Ācārya. Holding exquisite flowers in your hands and generating a heart of earnest devotion, receive the mantra orally from the Ācārya three times. If you are unable to receive it through recitation, you should write it down using paper and ox-gall (gorocana); having received it thus, you may recite it as you please.

"Once one has first entered the maṇḍala and subsequently received the mantra at another time, if one performs extensive offerings to the venerable ācārya on an auspicious day and receives it as before, one should know that this is the correct reception of the mantra and will swiftly attain accomplishment."
"Even if one performs the recitation without first performing the rite of service (*pūjā*), one will not achieve accomplishment.

Furthermore, take a new vessel free from defects and place within it leaves, the seven precious gems, and the five grains, each according to the ritual rules, but do not add water. With a heart of utmost sincerity, perform extensive offerings to the *ācārya*."
First, take paper leaves and write down the names of the various mantra-lords; place them inside a flask and perform offerings and adornments according to the *abhiṣeka* ritual.

While performing this, observe the fast and precepts for either one day or three days. At dusk, use ox-gall (*gorocanā*) to transcribe the names of the mantras and place them within the flask. Offer unguents, incense, lamps, and food, and perform the *homa* rite with the root mantra one hundred and eight times, diligently and extensively supplicating the noble assembly to listen attentively.

Listen attentively: for three days, have the disciple bathe until their body is fragrant; place an auspicious *kuśa* grass ring upon their hand, and with this mantra, recite it one hundred and eight times over the flask. Furthermore, fumigate it with incense, drink from it while performing prostrations at heart, and have them take a single leaf; having done so, they should again perform prostrations. One who receives [the initiation] in this manner will swiftly attain *siddhi*.
If, however, they additionally recite other mantras, the *siddhi* of the mantra they have received will be lost.

If one feels joy in the disciple’s heart and bestows upon them the *siddhi-mantra* held by oneself, the disciple should receive it according to the ritual rules and in accordance with the Dharma; because they have first recited and maintained it, the disciple will not fail to attain the *siddhi*.
"First, before the Lord of Mantras, present this petition and entrust this mantra, praying that he grant his empowerment to this disciple and swiftly bestow *siddhi*.
Holding incense and flowers in one's hands, recite it one hundred and eight or one thousand times, and then summon the disciple to receive it."
Having bestowed it, he further says these words:
"I now transfer this original primordial wisdom-lord to the disciple; I pray that you take note of this and grant me *siddhi*."
The disciple should say:
"I have now received the Illustrious Master; I vow that from this day forth until I attain enlightenment, I shall never neglect or forget [the teachings].
As stated above, when the master and disciple receive the mantra-dharma in this manner, they shall attain accomplishment; those who receive it otherwise shall not obtain *siddhi*.
Having thus received the *siddhi-mantra*, one will certainly achieve accomplishment therein without doubt.

One need not perform preliminary service (*puraścaraṇa*) for prior *siddhis*; since this is the case for mantras, it is likewise so for the methods of receiving medicinal substances and other *siddhis*.

Alternatively, there may be someone who first performs service, and subsequently, having combined recitation and retention according to the ritual rules, transmits it to another person; the one who receives it does not perform prior service, but achieves accomplishment simply by performing recitation and retention.

"Those who receive mantras, for the sake of attaining *siddhi*, should first extensively offer to their preceptor flowers, fruits, various roots, renowned garments and fine robes, gold, silver, *maṇi* gems, various miscellaneous precious objects, diverse grains and wheat, clarified butter, honey, milk, curd, male and female servants, various bedding, wondrous leather sandals, ornaments for the body, already perfected medicines, elephants, horses, oxen and calves, and other vehicles—even their own bodies—offering them as servants to be employed. Having served for a long time without fearing toil, they should offer with palms joined in devotion, with reverence and care; by practicing such giving, one swiftly attains *siddhi*."
It should be stated as follows: one must first offer the various aforementioned items to the Ācārya, and only thereafter [proceed] with the sublime phrases of the mantra.

Chapter Twenty-Three: The Chapter on the Fulfillment of Mantras from the Susiddhikara Sūtra. "Furthermore, if the practitioner of recitation sees the Lord of the Mantra in a dream, he should know that if the limbs of the deity's body are increased, the syllables of the mantra have been increased;
if the limbs are diminished, he should know that the syllables of the mantra are deficient. Having thoroughly understood these signs, he should perform the rite of fulfillment."

If one perceives that the mantra differs from what was received and upheld, or if one fails to employ it due to adding or subtracting syllables, doubt will arise in the mind; therefore, one should perform the practice according to the ritual until it is complete.

First, write down the erroneous mantras on paper leaves using *gorocanā* (cow bezoar). Having performed the ritual offerings and protections for the Mantra King and his retinue according to the rules, place the mantras upon the seat of the Lord of Mantras. Then, taking firewood and following the original rite, perform the *homa* offering; however, use only clarified butter (*ājya*) as an auxiliary aid to seek the favor of the Mantra King. Thus, one should perform the *homa*.
Spread mats of cogon grass and first pay homage to the Honored Master of the Rite Department;
next, pay homage to the Mother of the Rite Department;
then pay homage to all Buddhas, making this invocation:
"May all Buddhas and the assembly of noble ones grant their assistance and protection.

Having made this supplication, he lay down upon the straw with his head facing east. Within his dream, the tutelary deity manifested a sign: on the paper leaf written with ox-gall, that which was deficient was now complete; the number of characters inscribed by the deity in ox-gall reached full measure, and even the addition or subtraction of strokes was clearly settled;
as for the mantras, they were not erroneous, and it was simply said that they were not erroneous.
Alternatively, one may receive instructions in a dream regarding fulfillment; based on this, one should perform rites of protection to eliminate obstructing spirits (*māra*).

Chapter 24: Increasing Power *Susiddhikara Tantra*, Chapter Twenty-Four: Increasing Power Furthermore, if one wishes to increase one's majestic power, one should perform *homa* offerings, using either ghee and honey, or occasionally milk, performing each separately.
Alternatively, one may perform homa with sesame seeds;
or perform homa with resin incense mixed with ghee;
or perform homa with lotus flowers mixed with ghee.
At times, one may use *sajjārasa*;

or, dwelling among the mountains, one may constantly consume the five pure substances (*pañcāmṛta*) and eat no other food. One should take one hundred thousand flowers of the appropriate class and offer them to the deity with two mantras;

likewise, for excellent unguents, incense, flowers, lamps, food, and so forth, one should recite the mantra one hundred and eight times for each. Performing this three times a day for three days, such offerings will increase one's spiritual power.
Alternatively, one may burn hard wood to serve as a lamp for three periods each day over the course of seven days; this can cause the mantra to increase in power.
Or, by occasionally offering *gamika* food, the power is likewise increased.
The rules for recitation, *homa*, and offering as described above can likewise increase their power. Chapter 25:

The Chapter on *Homa*. In the Susiddhikara Sūtra, the twenty-fifth chapter on *Homa* states: "Furthermore, the rules for *homa* are explained in detail so that the practitioner may swiftly attain *siddhi*."

In front of the honored image, construct a homa hearth; it should be one cubit square at the top, with four sides and a depth of half a cubit. If a circular hearth is constructed, it should be made accordingly.

"If the place for recitation is within a chamber, one should go outside and gaze upon the form of the Honored One; there, having constructed a hearth, one should perform the rite according to the Dharma in accordance with the specific activity."

Place items such as milk-wood and fragrant flowers on the right side, and place the homa vessels on the left side. Sprinkle all the materials with the *rakṣā-mantra*, sit upon a seat of *kuśa* grass, and with a concentrated mind in meditative absorption, offer the *argha* while invoking the Vidyārāja; then pour a small amount of the *argha* water into the hearth.
Furthermore, offer one flower with each recitation of the mantra to the Lord of Mantras; to remove impurities, one should recite the Kīlikīli mantra and perform the hand gesture (mudrā);
for protection, recite the Kumbhira mantra and sprinkle water to purify the sacrificial wood and the fire.
Once the fire has been kindled, first invite the Fire Deity (Agni), saying:

"I now respectfully invite the foremost of fire deities, the sage among gods, who is honored by those who practice the holy life (brahmacarya); please descend to this place to accept and receive the homa."

Next, recite the mantra for summoning the Fire God as before; having thus named the Fire God, first purify with argha water three times. Taking the five grains, ghee, curd, and other substances, perform homa by reciting the mantra three times. The mantra for making offerings to the Fire God is the same as above.
Offer food to the Fire Deity with single-minded visualization, successively sending it to the Fire Deity and placing him upon his original seat.
Then, recite the Kilikili mantra and perform the mudrā to further purify the fire; all homa rites should be conducted in this manner.
Next, invite the tutelary deity; first recite the deity’s mantra once, then settle into the primary seat and perform the offerings according to the ritual:
"May the Honored One graciously accept this food for the homa."
"As for the wood for the homa ritual, it refers to:

the *pāralu* wood, the *udumbara* wood, the *bhallātaka* wood, the *nyagrodha* wood, the *khadira* wood, the *argha* wood, the *vikaṅkata* wood, the *arghamrda* wood, the *kāśmīra* wood, the *śamyāpāmārga* wood, and the *aśvattha* wood."
Regarding these twelve kinds of wood, take branches two finger-widths in length and one *śaṅku* in thickness, all of which must be moist.
Those freshly harvested may be used for all *homa* rituals. Select those with straight stems;

examine their upper and lower ends and place them on a surface of fragrant water to wash them clean. With the fine end facing outward and the thick end toward oneself, dip both ends in clarified butter (*ghṛta*) and cast them into the hearth.

When performing the two rites of *śāntika* and so forth, one should first offer *piṇḍa* food according to the specific procedure of each respective rite and perform the *homa*; this ritual framework applies universally to all cases.
"Whenever you prepare food each day, first set aside one portion and place it before the Honored One; this should be taken for use prior to the *homa* rite.
When performing recitation (*japa*), place it between both hands at the level of the knees; during the *homa*, it should be done in the same manner."

Using a piece of agalloch wood four finger-widths long and as thick as the index finger, smear it with *sugandhaka* resin and perform one hundred and eight *homā* offerings; this is the majestic empowerment of the *Svastyayana-mantra*.

When performing it in this manner, it is universally applicable to all sections of the tantras; alternatively, one may perform one hundred and eight *homa* offerings using *guggulu* incense mixed with clarified butter (*sarpis*).
At that time, one may also use *sajjarasa* for the *homa*, performing it one hundred and eight times; in all cases, these will increase the power and efficacy of the mantra.

"To accomplish the mantra-dharma, one performs various homas: first, invite the Lord of the Family (kula-nātha), then invite the Principal Deity (iṣṭadevatā), and thereafter perform the homa according to the ritual rules.

To accomplish the mantra-dharma, one performs the homa: first, use the mantra of the Family Mother (kula-mātṛ) to protect the Principal Deity and then protect oneself, and thereafter perform the homa according to the ritual rules.
To accomplish the mantra, one performs the homa; when the rite is concluded, in order to augment the power of the mantra, one should recite the Heart-mantra (hṛdaya-mantra) of the Family."

One performs homa for the purpose of accomplishing the protection mantras; at the beginning, one must always use the large ladle to offer oblations, and when nearing completion, one likewise uses the large ladle, while during the interval between, one should use the small ladle.
One performs various homas for the purpose of accomplishing the mantra methods; when the ritual is concluded, one makes offerings using the *kulahrdaya* (family-heart) mantra and mantra-arghya water.
"Just as the homa is protected within the methods of the maṇḍala, the sequential performance of the rites should also be conducted in this manner:
first perform the ābhicāruka rite, next perform the pauṣṭika rite, and next perform the śāntika rite."
When the homa is completed, use water purified by the root mantra to sprinkle it from afar around the hearth with the hand.

When the homa has been performed three times in this manner, once again address the Fire God (Agnideva) to receive further offerings. Then, according to the ritual, perform the dismissal and send him forth while reciting the aspiration prayers; as in the rite of invocation, replace the word for "descending" with the word for "departing."
Combine the remaining grains, ghee, honey, curd, and so forth into a single vessel, and perform *homa* by reciting the mantra of the Fire Deity three times;
then recite the root mantra according to its specific number of syllables;
finally, perform offerings and provide protection for the deity and yourself, and dismiss the deity according to the ritual rules.
26. Chapter on Requisite Articles, the Twenty-sixth of the Susiddhikara Sūtra. "Furthermore, the various branches of accomplishment are explained in detail.
That is to say, in order to accomplish all mantras, one should first prepare various miscellaneous materials and then perform the preliminary service (*pūrvasevā*).
If the preliminary service has already been performed, one should next engage in recitation, namely:
various types of unguents and various types of incense for burning.
"There are five kinds of solid incense,
namely: agallochum, white sandalwood, red sandalwood, sāla-wood, and celestial wood."
"The seven resinous incenses are: gandharasa, sājjarasa, guggulu, spṛkkā, turuṣka, sallakī, and śrīveṣṭaka."
White mustard seeds, poison, salt, black mustard seeds, sesame oil, cow’s ghee, a copper jar, and a copper ladle.
“The five grains refer to:
barley, wheat, rice, small beans, and sesame.”
"The five treasures are:
gold, silver, pearls, conch shells, and red pearls.
The five medicines are:"
The *khaṇḍakāri* medicine, the *vṛhatī* medicine, the *saha* medicine, the *sahadeva* medicine, and the *śatāvarī* medicine.
"Honey and five-colored threads— namely, blue, yellow, red, white, and black. A youth, a joined thread, a vajra, a lamp wick, a lamp bowl,

a clay vessel, a bowl, five kinds of colored pigments, a mortar made of khadira wood, a ladle made of milky wood, ox-gallstone, high-carbon steel, purple sandalwood, a purification cord, a bathing robe, a black deerskin, *bhaṅgā* flowers, rice blossoms, wooden sandals, *śaṅkha* grass, great reeds, *śatapuṣpā* (reverted fragrance), a flower basket for gathering blossoms, and various items required for food and drink such as clarified butter, honey, granulated sugar, rock sugar, and so forth, as well as grain beads."
One should prepare all the various items as described above; thereafter, one should perform the preliminary service (*pūrvasevā*) and extensive recitation (*japa*). Chapter 27:

On the Accomplishment of All Signs The Susiddhikara Sūtra, Chapter Twenty-Seven: On the Accomplishment of All Signs "Furthermore, I shall now explain the articles for accomplishment (*siddhi-dravya*), by which the *siddhi* of the mantras of these three families is attained."
They are as follows:
the cintāmaṇi jewel, the precious vase, the rain of jewels, the hidden treasure, the wheel, the yellow orpiment, and the sword.

These seven objects are the most supreme among the supreme; they can cause all kinds of siddhis to be accomplished and increase one's merit and virtue, even bringing to fulfillment the dharma of the Dharma King—how much more so other worldly matters?

The mantras of the three families—the Buddha Family, the Lotus Family, and the Vajra Family—all possess such supreme accomplishments; among these three families, whoever upholds them shall fully attain the five supernormal powers as the highest siddhi.
"Regarding the 'seven items': if one wishes to accomplish the Cintāmaṇi, once the ritual efficacy has been realized, one should fashion a golden pedestal measuring one cubit in length;

alternatively, one may use silver to craft it with exquisite ornamentation. Upon the head of the pedestal, place a maṇi-jewel; this jewel should be made of red crystal (*lohitaphala*), radiant, pure, and free from obscurations.
Or, using fine crystal, it should be perfectly fashioned according to the rite. Once this treasure is completed, one should perform recitation."
The design for the altar platform is not included here.

"If one wishes to accomplish the rite for raining down jewels, once the efficacy of the rite has been realized, by merely maintaining a sincere heart, gold, silver, and various miscellaneous jewels will rain down within a radius of five *yojanas*."

"If one wishes to accomplish the attainment of hidden treasures (nidhi), so as to provide gold, silver, and various jewels to relieve the poor and destitute, with all manner of expenditures, the treasury shall never be exhausted.

"If one wishes to accomplish the Wheel-Sage (cakravartin) rite, one should fashion a wheel from tempered iron, measuring two finger-widths and one span (vitasti) in circumference; the wheel should be equipped with six spokes and a rim, with the tips being sharp and keen."
By performing the ritual in this manner, one will swiftly attain siddhi.

"If one wishes to accomplish the rite of yellow orpiment, one should take 'radiant' orpiment that is like the sun at its rising; its color and luster should also be like the light of molten gold—this is considered the finest quality."

"If one who has mastered the art of the sword takes a fine blade of tempered steel, measuring two cubits in length—measured by the span of the little finger—and four fingers in width, free from all blemishes or defects, its color being a deep azure like that of the *cāmīkara* bird's beak."

"If one wishes to accomplish the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa rite, one should fashion a Buddha-uṣṇīṣa out of gold, just as it is depicted in a painting, and place it upon a pedestal; the pedestal and the cloth should be made of sphaṭika (crystal) gems."
"If one wishes to accomplish the Lotus Dharma, one should fashion an eight-petaled lotus from gold, measuring two finger-widths or one span;
or one may use silver;
or wrought copper; or white sandalwood."
"If one wishes to accomplish the Vajra rite, one should fashion a vajra from high-quality wootz steel, sixteen finger-widths in length, with three prongs at each end;
or it may be made of red sandalwood;
or it may be made of the Three Jewels—namely:"
Gold, silver, and refined copper.

"If one wishes to accomplish the rite of realgar, one should take realgar that is yellow like a mass of molten gold, which, when broken apart, again displays a luster upon its surface; such realgar can accomplish the aforementioned task."
"If one wishes to accomplish the rite of ox-gallstone (*gorocanā*), one should take the gallstone of a yellow cow as the best.
If one wishes to accomplish the *kālīka* medicine, one should take that medicine which is the color of a golden-coin flower (*dīnāra-puṣpa*) as the most excellent."
"If one wishes to accomplish the *sruva-anna* medicine, that which resembles earthworm dung is the best.
If one wishes to accomplish white cotton cloth, take fine and soft material, remove all hair and filth, and dye it with saffron."

"If one wishes to accomplish the protective thread (*rakṣāsūtra*), take fine strands of white cotton cloth and twist them into three strands; then, combine those three strands into a cord. A young girl should twist them together, ensuring all combinations are made from right to left;
alternatively, one may use gold threads."
"If one wishes to accomplish the rite of flower garlands, one should take *jāti* flowers and fashion them into a garland.
If one wishes to accomplish the rite of cow-dung ash, one should take pure cow dung from a forest hermitage (*araṇya*), burn it to produce white ash, and mix it with *kakkola* (camphor) incense."
"If one wishes to perform the rite for the accomplishment of wooden sandals, one should take *śrīparṇī* wood to make the sandals and place a canopy upon them.
"If one wishes to accomplish the rite for the parasol, it should be made with peacock feathers, and its flower should be made from fresh, high-quality bamboo."
"If you wish to accomplish the mastery of bows, arrows, spears, halberds, single-pronged forks, clubs, and all other weapons used according to worldly custom, you may fashion them as you please.

If you wish to accomplish the mastery of worldly saddled horses, chariots, oxen, sheep, all birds, beasts, and other such things, you may fashion them as you please—just as they are commonly regarded as superior by worldly people—or you may construct them according to the original ritual manual."

"If one wishes to achieve the accomplishment of a Vetāla, one should take the corpse of one born of a noble family, who died suddenly in the prime of youth and without illness, whose body shows no signs of discoloration, has not yet begun to bloat or decay, and whose sense faculties remain intact; having taken such a corpse, one should perform the accomplishment."

Whatever superior, middling, or inferior rites one performs according to one’s inclination, the objects to be taken are likewise so; one should perform these rites only when the mind is free from fear.
Chapter 28: Chapter on Taking Objects from the Susiddhikara Sūtra. "Furthermore, I shall now explain the method for taking objects. [The text continues as follows:]..."
On the eighth, fourteenth, and fifteenth days of both the waxing and waning moon, at the time of a solar eclipse, or during an earthquake—one should collect these substances on such days before noon;
or having attained a meditative state (*viṣaya*) during the time of recitation, one should collect them;
or, having purified oneself through bathing and observing the fast (*upavāsa*) without eating, one should seek a favorable meditative state and collect them.
Regarding the various items mentioned, wherever they may be located, if one possesses such items and they constitute precious goods, one should take them without paying their price;
or, at times when one perceives an increase in one's own power and is able to endure hunger, cold, and various other hardships, one should take those items at such a time.

Regarding all those objects, each according to its own nature, one should select the best among the superior, middling, and inferior grades; having obtained them in accordance with the Dharma, one should apply diligent effort to perform the rite of accomplishment.
Chapter 29: The Chapter on Purification. *Susiddhikara Sūtra*, Chapter Twenty-nine: The Chapter on Purification. Furthermore, I shall now explain the method for purifying various objects.
Those that may be washed should be cleansed with the five purifiers (*pañcagavya*); those that should not be washed should be sprinkled with the five purifiers.
Observe the proportions of the five pure substances to be ground into powder:
realgar mixed with milk to form a powder;
vermilion mixed with cow dung to form a powder; and so forth.
One should grind cow bezoar with *sū* (ghee) to make a powder, mixing it with pigments and milk;
however, for the *āñjana* medicine, one should simply prepare it as a powder.

Objects such as knives and wheels should be washed with water mixed with cow dung; as for other items mentioned that require washing, they should first be washed with cow urine and subsequently washed with scented water.

All other objects and such that are commonly used in the world should be washed with water; having washed them with scented water, one should next purify them by sprinkling with water consecrated by the *sarvakarmika-mantra*;
next, purify them by sprinkling with water consecrated by the *kulahṛdaya-mantra*;
and next, purify them by sprinkling with water consecrated by the *kuleśvarī-mantra*.
However, those things that require washing should first be washed with the five pure substances, followed by sesame-water, and then with scented water;
whatever requires purification should be treated in this manner. Chapter Thirty:

On the Quantities of Substances The Susiddhikara Sūtra, Chapter Thirty: On the Quantities of Substances "Furthermore, to explain in detail the substances for accomplishment: these refer to bodily ornaments, various weapons, and diverse garments according to worldly custom. Regarding the quantities used, one should grind them into fine powder and perform the rite of accomplishment."
"If one wishes to accomplish the rite of yellow arsenic (*haritāla*), five *liang* is the superior method, three *liang* is the middling method, and one *liang* is the inferior method.
"If one wishes to accomplish the rite of ox-gallstone (*gorocanā*), one *liang* is the superior method, half a *liang* is the middling method, and one part is the inferior method."
"If one wishes to accomplish the *añjana* rite, three parts constitute the superior method, two parts the middling method, and one part the inferior method.
"If one wishes to accomplish the *ghṛta* (ghee) rite, seven *liang* constitute the superior, five *liang* the middling, and three *liang* the inferior method."
"If one wishes to accomplish the rite of ashes, five *liang* is the superior method, three *liang* is the middling, and two *liang* is the inferior.
If one wishes to accomplish the rite of saffron, the quantity should be comparable to that of realgar."

Regarding the various methods for accomplishing medicinal pills within the *anuttana* ritual, one must prepare twenty-one pills for the superior method, fifteen pills for the middling method, and seven pills for the inferior method.
"In the case of this ritual manual, if the quantity of various items is small, one should increase their number; or follow the total quantity [of the original];
or follow the original manual;
or one may also rely on the quantities, whether many or few, that are esteemed in the world."

One should contemplate the power of recitation and visualization, as well as the number of companions; one must possess a state such as that of the retinue of the deity’s grace, for all accomplishments (*siddhi*) can be achieved accordingly. The methods for *siddhi* are categorized as superior, middling, and inferior, and the quantities of the various substances are likewise so.

Chapter Thirty-one: The Consecration Mandala. From the Susiddhikara Sūtra, Chapter Thirty-one: The Consecration Mandala. "Furthermore, I shall explain in detail the secret and wondrous methods for accomplishing all things, so that swift siddhi may be attained."

If one wishes to initiate the rite of accomplishment (*sādhana*), one should first prepare the requisites for protecting the *siddhi*. Then, performing the fire offering (*homa*) according to the mantra of the venerable deity and one's own consecration, one should construct a consecration maṇḍala and perform the offerings according to the ritual rules. Having completed the consecration, one may then begin the rite of accomplishment.

"If one constructs the Great Consecration Maṇḍala, one will be able to accomplish all matters; as previously explained, the methods for purifying the ground and so forth for the Maṇḍala of the Vidyārāja should all be performed in this same manner."

"That maṇḍala must be square with four corners and provided with four gates; its dimensions shall be eight cubits, seven cubits, or five cubits. Only the boundary paths (sīmā-mārga) are opened, and it is to be decorated with the five colors according to the rules. Following the measurement of the central terrace, the outer layer is reduced by half, and the subsequent outer layers are likewise proportioned."

"To the west of this, four cubits away, construct another maṇḍala measuring five, four, or three cubits; it should have its eastern gate opened according to the same principle, or be made at half the size of the location for the consecration of the fundamental great maṇḍala."

Generally, it is taught that for the site of a maṇḍala, a downward slope toward the north is auspicious; however, a site where the maṇḍala grounds slope downward toward the north is said to be the most excellent.
"Alternatively, one may paint it using a single color; at each of the four corners outside, draw a three-cubit *vajra*;
within the central platform, draw an eight-petaled lotus flower according to the ritual rules. All maṇḍalas should be made in this same manner."
Around the perimeter outside the lotus petals, draw auspicious and wondrous seals;
at the four gates, draw vajras;
furthermore, place auspicious vases at all corners; do the same for the outer abhiṣeka maṇḍala.

"Those who wish to perform the consecration must employ four types [of vessels]. The locations where the vases are placed should all be at the corners of the boundary. According to the mantras and vidyās being recited, one should draw the mudrā of the principal deity within the altar and place a vase there; for the mantra being held, one should draw the mudrā of the presiding deity of that particular family—namely, those of the Buddha-Usnīṣa, the Lotus, or the Vajra families."
One should know that this teaching is to be kept secret.

For those who do not know the name or the family (kula) of the mantra they hold, or for those who have not mastered it, one should place a single flask called "Accomplisher of All Tasks" (Sarvakarmika),
or a flask for the attainment of success and benefit (siddhārtha).
Alternatively, one may place a single flask and recite the mantra for inviting [the deity].
Next, on the outside facing east, draw the seal of the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa.
To its right, draw the seal of the Family Mother (Kulamātṛ), and beside that seal, the seal of the Family Heart (Kulahrdaya).
Next, on the right, place the seal of Śāriputra; next, on the left, the five seals;
next, on the right, Ānanda; and next, on the left, Subhūti.
As for the remaining mantras, vidyās, and so forth, their seals should be arranged on the left and right, extending even to the two corners.
"Next, on the northern side, draw the mudrā of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva;
on the right side, the mudrā of the Family Mother (Kulīśvarī), and on the left, the mudrā of the Family Heart (Kulahr̥daya);
next to the right, the mudrā of Lokeśvara, and next to the left, the mudrā of Tārā."
Next, on the right, place the mudrā of the Bodhisattva Siddhārtha; next, on the left, the mudrā of the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta.
As for the mudrās of all other mantras and vidyās, they are to be arranged on the left and right, extending even to the two corners.
"Next, on the southern side, paint the Vajra-mudrā;
on its right, the mudrā of the Family Mother (Kulīśvarī), and on its left, the mudrā of the Family Heart (Kulacitta);
next to the right, the Vajramuṣṭi-mudrā, and next to the left, the Vajrabhakṣa-mudrā."
Next, on the right, place the Vajra mudrā; next, on the left, the Vajra-muṣṭi mudrā.
As for the mudrās of all other mantras and vidyās, they are to be arranged on the left and right, extending even to the two corners.
"Next, on the south side of the western gate, draw the seal of Brahmā and the Vidyārāja Brahmaśrī, together with their retinues;
continuing thus, at the north side of the southern corner gate, draw the seal of the deity Rudra and the seal of his consort, together with their retinues;
and finally, at the third mandala gate of the northern corner, draw the deities of the eight directions, each with their respective retinues, so as to fill their positions."
Outside the gate of the second maṇḍala, draw the Nāga King Sunanda on the right side and the Nāga King Upananda on the left side;
outside the gate of the third maṇḍala, draw the Nāga King Sunda on the right side and the Nāga King Upasunda on the left side; and outside the maṇḍala, draw the seal of the Amṛta jar.

"One who performs the Dharma-offering of the maṇḍala in this manner should perform three kinds of homa according to the ritual rules: one should perform the ābhicāruka rite for the purpose of expelling the vināyakas;
one should perform the pauṣṭika rite for the sake of one's own benefit;
and one should perform the śāntika rite for the purpose of pacifying all calamities and malevolent influences."

One should perform the *ābhicāruka* rites using the *sarvakarmasādhana-mantra* of the respective family, or alternatively, use the *amṛtakuṇḍalī-mantra*, which may be employed across all three families;
one should perform the *pauṣṭika* rites using the *hṛdaya-mantra* of the respective family;
and one should perform the *śāntika* rites using the *mātṛkā-mantra* of the respective family.
To the noble ones assembled in the maṇḍala and all the devas, one should perform the threefold homa with their respective root mantras;
or one may perform the homa with the mantra for accomplishing all activities.

At the site of the homa, to the east of the southern gate of the maṇḍala, one should prepare substances such as ghee according to the homa ritual. To augment the power of the various mantras, one should perform these three types of homa by reciting the three essential mantras one hundred times each, or for a certain number of times.

Subsequently, one should offer seven oblations for each mantra of the three families; however, the lords of the three families should be offered more oblations. Alternatively, one may simply offer one hundred oblations to the three families; if this is not possible, seven or even three oblations will suffice.
"The mantra-holders one possesses should be placed beneath the feet of the central deity within the inner maṇḍala.
Outside the maṇḍala, place Hārītī separately on the eastern side;
place Śūlinī on the southern side."
Place Ekajaṭā on the west side;
place Cundā on the north side, and offer them whatever they delight in.
Having performed the ritual offerings to the mantras and the homa, empower the previously established flask with the recitation of the appropriate mantra for the purpose at hand.
The vases placed before the deity should be consecrated using that same mantra;
the vases within the central platform should be consecrated using the mantra of the Vidyārāja;
and the vase installed by Cundā at the entrance must likewise be consecrated with her mantra.
Regarding the vases placed at the eastern and western corners of the platform maṇḍala: for the northeast corner, use the Family Heart Mantra;
for the southeast corner, use the Family Mother Mantra;
and for the northwest corner, use the Mantras of Accomplishment.
For the southwest corner, one should employ all mantras.
Having thus consecrated this superior vase and performed the offerings, one should next circumambulate it clockwise.
The method for conferring empowerment as previously described applies here as well; in this manner, one should install the auspicious vase (śrīkalaśa), namely:
Place grains, medicinal herbs, flowers, fruits, branches and leaves from fragrant trees, flower garlands, and jewels inside the flask, and wrap its neck with new silk and colored cloth.
All empowerment rites should be performed in this manner.

One should then have a companion empower the practitioner on the crown of the head; such companions must all maintain the recitation and be pure according to the Dharma, or else one should request the Ācārya to bestow the empowerment upon them.
In order to dispel all obstacles to one's activities, one should first perform the consecration using the Kuntali flask;
for the fourth, one should use the flask held by the deity while reciting its mantra; as for the remaining two flasks, they may be used according to one’s preference.
When this is completed, one should employ ox-gall (*gorocanā*), unguents, incense, mustard seeds, thread bracelets, and garments for use.
After performing the consecration (*abhiṣeka*), one should perform *homa* to pacify all obstacles, and then immediately dismiss [the deity].

Alternatively, in a pure place, using only a single color, one should construct a small maṇḍala that is perfectly square and two cubits in measure. One should install the great mudrās of the three obstructions; on the western side, the spear mudrā should be installed as before. By performing the empowerment according to the ritual with the pure flask, one will be freed from all obstructions. The tutelary deity will be pleased, and before long, one will swiftly attain this most supreme secret siddhi.

32. Chapter on Light Substances. *Susiddhikara Sūtra*, Chapter Thirty-Two: "Furthermore, once the ritual consecration (*abhiṣeka*) has been completed according to the Dharma, one should perform homa for twenty-one days, seven days, or one month;
or as appropriate for the specific accomplishment (*sādhana*). One should use ghee, honey, and curd mixed with sesame seeds at the three times of day as prescribed in the root text;
or, according to the root text, offer milk porridge."
Alternatively, one may offer curd-rice as a sacrifice.
The object to be accomplished should be incensed with fragrant smoke three times each day and sprinkled with scented water.
One should empower and gaze upon the object with mantras;
one should place a *śrīvatsa* amulet upon a finger and press it against the object;
one should sprinkle the object with ox-gall water or white mustard seeds; and on auspicious days, one should offer various ritual implements to that object.
If it is accomplished during the waxing moon, take the tenth day;

if it is accomplished during the waning moon, take the fourteenth day. When performing such rites to cause the object to manifest its radiance, one should employ the mantra of the Family Mother (Kulamātṛ) for all of them.

Furthermore, one should again increase the offerings with various flowers, incense, garlands, and other articles; having anointed the hands with incense and placed a ring of *kuśa* grass upon them, one should perform the recitation throughout the night once the object to be accomplished has been completed.

Recite one hundred and eight times during the three periods of the night; such is the manner in which the object of accomplishment should be manifested from beginning to end, for if one possesses this method, accomplishment will be swiftly attained.
The *Vairocana-mantra* of the Buddha Family:
“Oṃ tijaya seṃ-vini siddhi-sādhaya hūṃ phaṭ. The *Vairocana-mantra* of the Lotus Family:
“Oṃ jvālana-jvalini-pāya mahāśriye svāhā. The *Vairocana-mantra* of the Vajra Family is as follows:
"Oṃ jvala jvalaya pāṇḍurī svāhā. For all rites of the three families (*trikula*), one should use red *karavīra* flowers; reciting the mantra, one should scatter and sprinkle them over the objects.
Alternatively, one may use *mallikā* flowers or white mustard seeds; at the beginning, end, and middle, one should likewise scatter and moisten the objects in this manner.
If there are visionary realms or the appearance of extraordinary signs, one should likewise scatter [the offerings].
When one is about to achieve accomplishment, one should likewise scatter [the substances], and they will then become radiant and manifest.
If one wishes to accomplish substances such as ghee, one should sprinkle them with mantra-empowered perfumed water, and they will then become radiant and manifest.
One should illuminate all things with such dharmas, and even if success is not achieved, one must not interrupt the practice.
To illuminate by means of a maṇḍala, one should prepare the site as previously described and construct a maṇḍala using five colors; it should measure four cubits and have a single gate.
"In the eastern side of the inner court, first place the wheel seal;
in the northeast corner, place the bowl seal;
and in the southeast corner, place the robe seal."
"Next, place the lotus mudrā in the north;
place the ḍamaru-staff mudrā in the northwest corner;
and place the kamaṇḍalu-bottle mudrā in the northeast corner."
"Next, place the Vajra mudrā on the southern side;
place the Gada mudrā in the southeast corner;
and place the Kalaśa mudrā in the southwest corner."
"On the western side, place the Vajrāṅkuśa mudrā and the Vajramuṣṭi mudrā;
in the southwest corner, place the Kīlikīla mudrā;
in the northwest corner, place the Śumbha mudrā."
Furthermore, on the right side of the wheel at the eastern face, place the seal of the Mother of the Buddha Family;
again, on the right side of the lotus seal at the northern face, place the seal of the Pañcarakṣā Family Mother;
and at the southern face, place the seal of the Vajra, with the seal of the Māmakī Family Mother placed on its right side.
Next, outside the gate of the maṇḍala, place the seal of Caṇḍamahāroṣaṇa, who can crush all hostile armies, as previously described, and perform offerings according to the preceding ritual.

Furthermore, on the northern side, place the seals of the Six-Armed One, Hayagrīva, Tārā, and Caṇḍanara; install all the retinues belonging to their respective families in successive order, their forms being entirely white.
Moreover, on the eastern side, place the seal of the Tathāgata Śakti, the seal of Tejorāśi, the seal of Aparājita-dvārapati, and the seal of Aparājita-vidyārājñī.
Furthermore, on the southern side, one should arrange all the retinues within their respective sections in successive order;
however, on the western side, one may install the various mudrās of the three families as one pleases.

"Next, place the great deities of the eight directions, such as Kuvira and others, in the outer enclosure; in the empty spaces thereof, place at will the mantra-lords who accomplish all matters within the three families.

Next, place a bamboo pole on the central platform; whatever objects have been accomplished through the mudrās of the family lords should be placed therein according to what is taught in the rites of their respective families, and the lord of that family should be installed there."
On the central platform, place the objects for the ritual beside the mantra-text and the mudrā one holds;
to the west of these objects, install the homa hearth.
Next, the reciter sits to the west, and each person invokes [the deities] according to the ritual rules using their respective root mantras.

Having completed the offerings as before, one should perform homa with the vidyās of the three families in succession to manifest the object, and then perform homa with the root mantra to bring about its manifestation.

"Among all methods for illumination (*prabhāsana*), *homa* is supreme. At the beginning of any *homa*, one should first consecrate the objects with perfumed water while reciting the *kula-mātṛ* mantra; once the *homa* is completed, one should likewise sprinkle them.
Alternatively, one may use the *maṃjughoṣa-hṛdaya-mantra* or the four-syllable *Vidyārāja* mantra to perform illumination for the *homa* of any of the three families."
Regarding the performance of homa according to the specific mantra used: first, one recites only that mantra; next, one recites the words of supplication;
then, in the middle, one again recites that mantra followed by the words of supplication;
and finally, one again recites that mantra, concluding with the words of supplication.

"In this manner, within the mantra, one should place the phrases of supplication in three sections—superior, middling, and inferior—and finally append the syllables 'hūṃ phaṭ svāhā,' which are the words of invocation."

“*Jvala* [cause to] emit light; *jvālaya* [cause to] emit light; *siddhi* [accomplish]; *sādhaya* [cause to] accomplish; *nidhīpa* [splendor]; *nibhaya nibhūtānām* [of those who are fearless]; *tejasa* [brilliance]; *vardhaya* [cause to] increase; *mā vilamba* [do not delay]; *aviśa* [enter everywhere]; *rakṣa* [protect]; *saṃnidhāpaya* [cause to appear before us as an omen]; *kuru* [do]; *hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*. By means of such phrases of invocation, one illuminates the object; it is likewise no hindrance to recite them variously in repetition at the beginning, middle, or end.”
When the homa is completed, one should next recite mantras while scattering white karavīra flowers over the objects to consecrate them with radiance;
alternatively, one may use red karavīra flowers, white mustard seeds, or sumana flowers to effect this consecration.
First, apply scented ointment to the hands and press them against the object;
next, hold various flowers while reciting the mantra and scatter white mustard seeds;
then, burn incense to fumigate it.
Thereafter, one should recite [the mantra] and sprinkle it with scented water.

It should be understood that this sequence is performed during the three periods of the night—the first, middle, and last watches—sprinkling with scented water while reciting the mantra of the primary treasury-lord (*kośapati*), followed by reciting the primary *dhāraṇī* mantra. Having completed the sprinkling, one performs the *homa* and recitation as before until sunrise. One who possesses this method will swiftly attain accomplishment.

"By thus illuminating various objects as well as one's own body, one will certainly and swiftly achieve accomplishment regarding those objects; even if the objects are few, one will obtain great efficacy."

One who possesses this dharma will see their possessions increase and attain purity; therefore, one should perform the rite of illumination. This is called the secret dharma of universal accomplishment.
"On all festival days, one should perform such rites of illumination; on other days, one may perform them as the occasion arises.

Once the required number of recitations has been completed, when one wishes to perform the rite of accomplishment (*sādhana*), one must first fully perform the rite of illumination during the first watch of the night before proceeding to the accomplishment."
Susiddhikara Sūtra, Middle Volume;
Susiddhikara Sūtra, Lower Volume.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Śubhakarasiṃha of India during the Tang Dynasty.

Chapter Thirty-Three: Distinguishing the Times for Attaining Siddhi Furthermore, I shall now explain the auspicious times for accomplishment; once the practitioner has understood this, they should seek siddhi.
Regarding the seasons:

in the eighth month, the twelfth month, the first month, the second month, and the fourth month—on the fifteenth day of the waxing moon in these five months, one should perform the supreme accomplishment (*uttamasādhana*).
In the fourth month, there will inevitably be the difficulty of rain;
in the second month, there will inevitably be the difficulty of wind;
and in the first month, there will inevitably be various kinds of difficulties.
Only the twelfth month is free from all difficulties;
during the eighth month, there are the perils of snow, hail, and thunderbolts.
As described above, these aforementioned perils are all signs of accomplishment.

During these five months, one should only seek to perform rites of accomplishment (*sādhana*); one should also perform *śāntika* rites. Specifically, on the fifteenth day of the dark fortnight of this fifth month, one should perform the middle and lower grades of accomplishment rites;
one should also perform *pauṣṭika* and *abhicāruka* rites.
"One should accomplish the most supreme objects during a lunar eclipse;
one may accomplish objects of the superior, middling, and inferior grades during a solar eclipse;
or on the first, third, fifth, seventh, or thirteenth day of the lunar month, one should perform the accomplishment of all matters."
"If one performs the supreme accomplishment (*uttamasādhana*), one should select an auspicious time based on the lunar mansions (*nakṣatra*) and planets (*graha*),
or else act in accordance with the three types of ritual methods (*trividhakarmadharma*).
The accomplishment itself is also performed by relying on these three matters, or as explained in the specific root text."
Alternatively, one may follow the instructions of the tutelary deity (iṣṭadevatā).

Between the first and fifteenth days of the twelve months, all accomplishments and rites should be performed; or one may select the day indicated by the deity, or even the thirteenth day of either the waxing or waning moon in any month will yield accomplishment.
"The seventh and eighth months are the latter season of the rains; during this time, one should perform *śāntika* rites.
The ninth and tenth months are the early season of winter; during this time, one should perform *pauṣṭika* rites.
The third and fourth months are the latter season of spring; during this time, one should perform *abhicāruka* rites."
The first and second months are the initial seasons of spring; at this time, one should accomplish all matters.
The fifth and sixth months are the initial season of the rains; those who wish to achieve accomplishments (*siddhi*) should perform the lower *siddhis* during these months.

In this way, during the seasons of spring, winter, and after the rains, one should likewise accomplish the three types of *siddhi*. Within these, the nine grades are distributed according to their respective categories.
"At the first watch of the night, when there is accomplishment of the lower grade;
at the middle watch of the night, when there is accomplishment of the middling grade;"
During the latter part of the night, when the supreme accomplishment (*uttamasādhana*) is performed:
the first part of the night is the time for performing *śāntika* rites;
the middle part of the night is the time for performing *abhicāruka* rites.
Regarding the subsequent section on performing the pauṣṭika rites:

within these three matters, there are ninefold distinctions; one should know the appropriate timing according to their respective correspondences, and distinguish the superior, middling, and inferior qualities of the signs that appear during those periods.
Nevertheless, one should perform the rite precisely at the time of a solar or lunar eclipse, regardless of the specific hour.
For all rites of fierce accomplishment (*tīkṣṇa-sādhana*) and *abhicāruka* (subjugation), the time of a solar or lunar eclipse is most conducive.
In all cases at the commencement of an accomplishment (*sādhana*), one should fast for three days, two days, or one day;

it should be understood that these upper, middle, and lower grades correspond to the respective types of rites. Chapter Thirty-Four: The Chapter on Perfect Accomplishment (*Pariniṣpanna-siddhi-paṭala*). From the Susiddhikara Sūtra. Furthermore, I shall now explain the deficiencies in the branches of accomplishment regarding the fundamental rites (*mūla-vidhi*).

If you fear that your physical strength will not sustain you, do not practice total fasting. Once the required number of recitations has been completed and you wish to initiate the rite of accomplishment (*sādhana*), you must further perform recitations and *homa* offerings, making offerings of flowers and incense and praising the deity with various hymns while contemplating the *iṣṭadevatā*. Take a thread of white cotton and have a young girl join it together; perform the ritual as before, tying seven knots and reciting the mantra seven hundred times. At dawn, fasten it around your waist so that you do not lose semen in your dreams.
The mantra of the Buddha Family, the *Sukumāra* mantra:
“Oṃ jaye sukumāre vikrāntapade svāhā. The mantra of the Lotus Family, the *Durginī* mantra:
“Oṃ rukṣaṇa kuru durgini svāhā. The mantra of the Vajra Family, the *Māmakī* mantra:
"Oṃ kulanḍari bandha bandha huṃ phaṭ. Recite this mantra of invocation at the beginning, middle, and end of each session.

If the mantra of one's own root practice lacks a request for protection, one should take and append this [mantra] to it; however, these three vidyās are to be used according to their respective sections.
One should daily bind and wear the recitation cord while performing the ritual to make the practice radiant;
when constructing a maṇḍala, during recitation, and on auspicious days, it must be bound and worn to eliminate obstacles and hindrances.
Furthermore, for the eye-salve:

take equal parts of *sruva*, *añjana*, *śarkarā*, *karpūra*, *pippalī*, *jātīkośa*, *tvak*, and white raw honey; grind and sift them into a powder. Mix this with the foam from a horse’s mouth and pound it thoroughly. Then, recite this vidyā over it one hundred and eight times.

At the time of accomplishment, one should wash the face repeatedly and apply the medicine to the eyes; thereby, laziness and mental torpor are removed, and when obstacles arise, they are perceived in advance through dreams.
The mantra for the eye-union ointment of the Buddha Family is:
"Oṃ jvala rocani svāhā. The mantra for the eye-union ointment of the Lotus Family is:
"Oṃ milukini śava. The mantra for the eye-union ointment of the Vajra Family is:
"Oṃ bandhura-ijyapti svāhā. These three mantras are to be employed by the respective families.
By applying them to eye-salve or simply reciting them over water to wash the face and eyes several times, one may also eliminate the hindrance of torpor and sleep.
"If you become weary from recitation during the time of accomplishment, take white sandalwood mixed with water, recite the Family Heart Mantra over it seven times, and drink three handfuls.
When desiring to accomplish [the rite], first sprinkle your body with water; you should wait for auspicious signs before proceeding with the accomplishment."
Those possessing auspicious marks are as follows:
the high-bound wheel-hook-fish right-turning seal;
the white lotus banner; and so forth.
The *svastika* mudrā;
the full-vase and *śrīvatsa* mudrās;
the vajra and the flower garland.
Some see beautiful women adorned with necklaces and ornaments;
some see pregnant women or those carrying clothes and goods;
some see joyful young maidens.
Or they may see a pure-practicing Brahmin wearing fresh white garments;
or they may see them riding in chariots, on elephants, or horses, or carrying medicinal roots and fruits;
or they may see extraordinary occurrences.
Some hear the sound of thunder;
some hear the sound of Vedic recitation;
and some hear the sounds of conchs, horns, and various musical instruments.
Or they may hear the sounds of peacocks, partridges, parrots, cranes, and auspicious birds;
or they may hear the voices of kind words of consolation—words that begin with "May there be peace" and express the fulfillment of one's desires;
or they may see celebratory clouds, lightning, gentle breezes, and light rain.
Either flowers rain down from the heavens;
or there is excellent fragrance, or one sees halos and eclipses.
Among these signs, that which is bestowed by the heavens constitutes the supreme accomplishment.
Manifestation in space constitutes middling accomplishment;
manifestation on the ground constitutes inferior accomplishment.

Regarding these three signs, they are further distinguished into nine grades. As previously manifested, all of these are auspicious; however, that which is not seen therein constitutes non-accomplishment.
Having seen these signs, one should give rise to deep joy; with such a mind, one subsequently performs the ritual methods for accomplishment through skillful means.
Chapter Thirty-Five: Invoking Accomplishment (*Susiddhikara-sūtra*, Chapter Thirty-Five: Invoking Accomplishment). "Next, the method for invoking accomplishment shall be explained.
The aforementioned times, planetary positions, and auspicious signs have already been explained in detail within the rituals for constructing maṇḍalas and the methods for spiritual accomplishment.

"If inauspicious signs appear, one should immediately perform homa with cow ghee using the Mother of the Family mantra one hundred and eight times; thereafter, when performing the ritual, one will also attain the accomplishment of siddhi."
"One should also perform the accomplishment based on the previously described maṇḍala site.
For a superior accomplishment, one should perform it on a mountain;
for a middling accomplishment, one should perform it by the side of a pond."
The lower grade of accomplishment may be performed anywhere.
Alternatively, it may be performed at a place corresponding to a mantra; if one does not perform the accomplishment in such a place, it will be somewhat delayed.
If one performs it within a *caitya* containing bone relics (*śarīra*), all mantras of the Inner Dharma will attain accomplishment.
Among the eight great *caityas*, such as the place of the Buddha’s birth, this is the most supreme for attaining accomplishments (*siddhi*).

Furthermore, at the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*), no obstacles whatsoever can arise that would hinder one's attainment of accomplishment; even Māra does not create obstacles there, let alone other classes of beings.
Therefore, all mantras will certainly achieve accomplishment.
"Whatever fierce accomplishments there may be, they should be performed in a cemetery;
or else in an empty house."
One should perform the rite of accomplishment either in a temple where a single deity resides alone,
or beneath a solitary tree in a remote place, or by the side of a river.
"If one wishes to accomplish the rite of a female yakṣī, one should perform it in a forest;
if one wishes to accomplish the dharma of a nāga king, one should perform it by a spring;
if one wishes to accomplish the dharma of wealth and nobility, one should perform it upon the roof of a house."
If one wishes to accomplish the rite of the messenger (dūtī), one should perform it at a place where people gather;
if one wishes to accomplish the rite of entering caves, one should perform it within a cave.
This is the place for the secret accomplishment of discernment.

Having first attained the meditative concentration of discerning the ground, one should fast according to the ritual for purifying the site of a maṇḍala, or purify the ground according to the ritual for the recitation chamber; when the location is thus clean, spiritual efficacy is swiftly attained.
First, using the *Sarvakarmasādhana-mantra* or the *Kumārakrodha-mantra*, one should recite over white mustard seeds and other substances and scatter them upon the ground to ward off all obstacles.

Take four stakes made of khadira wood, each measuring two finger-widths; bend and conceal the ends so that one tip resembles a single-pronged pestle, and coat the stakes with red sandalwood-scented clay.
Then, wrap them with crimson thread.
Forming a fist with the Vajra-kila mudrā and holding it,
recite this mantra one hundred and eight times and drive [the kila] into the four corners so that the head of the kila is slightly visible.
Make a white banner and suspend it from a long bamboo pole at the eastern side of the maṇḍala.
Recite the Vajra-Wall mantra one hundred times over iron filings and fashion three-pronged vajras with their tips joined together to encircle the maṇḍala, serving as the vajra wall.
